ns2:section.sectionText: Border crossings: A study of transnational migrations. This course explores the global movement of people, examining root causes of transnational migration. A range of socio-cultural, economic, environmental, linguistic, and political factors will be explored. Topical case studies will include human trafficking, student mobility, hometown associations, diaspora and refugee populations, and the impact of climate change and global terrorism on border crossings. If this course is full call 217-333-0178 and ask to be put on a waitlist. As of 8-18-09 the major restriction has been removed.
